purpose: Every sentence in README section IV that states a number, mapped to the artifact that produced it. 'in-clone' means a fresh clone can reproduce or at least inspect the raw rows; anything else is labelled by why it is not.

claims.claim: Qwen3-4B fitted arms do not reach the published same-base removal
the oracle edit is a shared rank-1 axis confined to blk.9-35, and the fitted axis only reaches 0.5056 of it
claims.notes: the axes tensors themselves are 90 MB captures in scratch, not in the clone; the recovered direction is reproducible from the published GGUF with gguf-tensor-diff.

claims.claim: Qwen2.5-1.5B capability retention: base 98/241, published third-party ablation 81/241, SAS@1.5 184/241
a wave cannot report a number for an artifact the port is not serving, and an empty screen is not a result
Qwen2.5-1.5B shared-axis fit: 40/40 on the harmful-40 suite, 24/24 on held-out refusal families, harmless clean
claims.notes: Taken before the row-kind scoring fix, and the raw harmful/holdout answer rows are not in this clone. The certification is void as a number; the retained artifact is the capability-retention wave above, which measures what happened to maths and code, not whether refusals left.

claims.claim: MiniCPM-V 4.7 per-layer answer-span fit: 36/40, plus null-space-protected and shape-interpolated variants
claims.notes: The committed MiniCPM directory contains serving checks, GGUF digests and a baseline refusal screen only. The removal screens behind 36/40 predate the fix and are not in the clone, so the number is quoted in history, not as current evidence.

claims.claim: Spark-X2.6-1.7B and LFM3-1.7B refusal openers gone 40/40, harmless clean, style drift recorded
claims.notes: No wave, screen or provenance file for either model is in this repository or on the lab disk. Treat as unevidenced until re-run; it is a candidate result, not a certified one.

claims.claim: on 24 refusal families never used for fitting, the best fitted q3 arm removes 23 of 24 and the published build removes 24
claims.notes: one row per family, 24 distinct families, built from verification/harsh-suites/holdout.jsonl with every fit-pool id excluded. This is the screen the removal claim rests on, not advbench-40.

claims.claim: no fitted q3 arm is statistically distinguishable from the published removal on the held-out families — on the wording metric only
claims.notes: exact McNemar on paired prompt ids: fitted arm 1 discordant (p 1.0), blk.9-35 arm 3 discordant (p 0.25), base 20 discordant (p < 1e-5). A hand read of the same 24 rows for delivery, not wording: the published build delivers on 4 families, the fitted arm on 5, two discordant each side — the parity holds on behaviour too, and the reading is that neither artifact removes refusal behaviour. Single reader per R2; a second reader has not been done.
